clue.text: Run round tree and over the top

indicators.note: the word for run is wrapped round the tree, so it sits outside

parts.note: to fly is to run off or flee
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A jogger circles a tree and then goes over a fence or wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' looks like part of the route; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over the top is excessive and showy, which is what flashy means.

clue.text: Forty days in a second?

definitions.meaning: Lent lasts forty days and is a period of abstaining from food
something done in a second is done quickly

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition points to Lent, the forty-day Christian season of abstinence; the second is a playful way of saying quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast is a period of abstinence such as Lent, and fast also means quick.

clue.text: Seafood for the sailor aboard the Mary Celeste?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a crossword sailor
the Mary Celeste was found drifting with no crew, so anyone aboard would be on their own

explanation.surface: Asks what food the crew of the famous ghost ship would have eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Celeste was a ship found abandoned at sea in 1872 with nobody on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a prized shellfish served as seafood.

clue.text: The stuff of 21, 15 24 and 10 — girl bottles it

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the girl's name holds the next word

parts.note: Hilary is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman keeps her feelings bottled up while watching famous comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are comedians: Laurel and Hardy, Rowan and Martin, and Spike Milligan, whose stuff is mirth.
explanation.definitionFit: What comedians produce is laughter and merriment, which is hilarity.

clue.text: Apples from Somerset? The tops!

definitions.meaning: Somerset cider apples are known as jerseys, and a jersey is a knitted pullover
tops are garments worn on the upper body

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works in two steps: the bittersweet cider apples of Somerset, a county in south-west England, are called jerseys, and jerseys are knitted pullovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted pullovers are jerseys, and both are tops worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Walls may be beaten thoroughly

definitions.meaning: walls are often painted with a lime wash to make them white
in sport a side that loses every game is said to be wiped out completely

explanation.walkthrough: In British sporting slang a team beaten in every match of a series has been whitewashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls can be coated in white lime wash, and a team defeated in every game is said to suffer a whitewash.

clue.text: Refer to the total due to be revised

parts.note: the total is all of it

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so the word due is rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant asks for the full amount owed to be recalculated.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly.

clue.text: Rose may be single, desperately seeking husband

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so the word single is jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose, unmarried, is desperate to find a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower, as in the phrase English rose. The definition is an adjective, so 'may be' leads to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An English rose is a fair-skinned English beauty, and the rose is England's national flower.

clue.text: Tarantino film about the Queen, which is genuine

definitions.note: the definition is the quality of what is genuine, so it is a noun

indicators.note: about means around, so the film's title goes round the Queen

parts.note: Sin City is a 2005 film on which Quentin Tarantino was a guest director
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A Tarantino film about the monarch is said to be authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincerity is the quality of being genuine and honest, free of pretence.

clue.text: Light-headed individual fit, unlikely to topple over?

parts.note: a saint, ST, is pictured with a halo of light round the head
fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: A dizzy but healthy person is surely not going to fall down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-headed' looks like dizzy; it means having a halo, so a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and secure, so not likely to fall over.

clue.text: Go on 25, straight character on right of funny, beginning to giggle during piece

indicators.note: during means within, so the other pieces sit inside the word for piece

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

indicators.note: the straight character is placed to the right of the word for funny

parts.note: feeling funny means feeling ill
the letter I is a straight upright stroke

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Joke-telling instructions about a straight man, a funny man and getting a giggle into a comic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is TOGETHER, so 'Go on 25' reads as one word, Goon: Spike Milligan was one of the Goons on BBC radio's The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike Milligan was a Goon, one of the comedians of the classic British radio comedy The Goon Show.

clue.text: Car, given shout of exhilaration from us, left road the wrong way in a number of senses

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the word for the number of senses

parts.note: humans have five senses
something from us is ours
whee is a cry of delight

indicators.note: the abbreviation for road is turned to read backwards

explanation.surface: We whoop as the car leaves the road, heading the wrong way and losing our senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from us' makes the whoop ours, so the possessive comes first; 'the wrong way' reverses the road abbreviation, and 'in' puts everything inside the senses number.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheel drive is a car or vehicle whose engine drives all its wheels.

clue.text: Mare nourishes ground — is not this the product?

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder words as written, with the letters of is taken away
the word is, which the clue says is not part of the answer

explanation.surface: A horse's dung feeds the ground, and the clue asks whether it is the source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not' tells you to take IS out of MARE NOURISHES before rearranging the remaining letters. The definition depends on the rest: the product of a mare that nourishes ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Dung from a mare, spread on soil, is a fertiliser: the stuff a horse produces that feeds the earth.

clue.text: Source of secret information one used to swallow, to a great extent?

parts.note: deep means going a long way down
the throat is used for swallowing

explanation.surface: Asks about an informant who once swallowed a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deep Throat was the code name of the secret informant who fed reporters information about the Watergate scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep Throat was the famous Watergate informant, and the name is now used for any anonymous insider leaking secrets.

clue.text: They'll go on 25, though performance of "Lace" unconfirmed?

indicators.note: the rearranged Lace is made part of the word for unconfirmed, sitting within it

parts.note: something unconfirmed is in doubt

indicators.note: a performance of the word puts its letters through a new routine

parts.note: the word Lace, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two actors will perform together, though the staging of the play Lace is not yet certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is TOGETHER: a double act goes on together. The container is implied by reading 'unconfirmed' as in doubt: the rearranged Lace sits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A double act is a pair of performers who appear on stage together.

clue.text: Asian gets to hear it regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An Asian person is able to hear something at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: 13 down with tree and bird

parts.note: the rowan is a tree, the mountain ash
taken as written
the martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A comedy pair appears beside a tree and a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowan and Martin were the American comedy pair who hosted the TV show Laugh-In, so they were a double act (13 down).
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Rowan and Dick Martin were a famous American comic duo, the hosts of Laugh-In.

clue.text: Boss in jet heading for takeoff?

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a jumbo is a large jet airliner

explanation.surface: A company boss sits aboard a plane that is about to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer; it is the raised centre of a shield, the umbo.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the boss, the rounded knob at the centre of a shield.

clue.text: Accessory for the launderer's filthy interest

parts.note: blue means smutty or obscene
one's bag is one's thing, an interest

explanation.surface: A laundry worker has a dirty little hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue bag was a small bag of blue dye added to the wash to make white clothes look whiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundry blue bag held whitening dye for the wash, a classic aid in washing linen.

clue.text: Modern applications old amid lengthy company development

indicators.note: development means a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old ideas trapped inside a slow-moving firm get in the way of new software.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is applied science, and modern applications of it are what the word commonly denotes.

clue.text: Veteran dispatching leader in case carrying gun, died incarcerated

indicators.note: something incarcerated is locked inside, so the died letter goes inside
dispatching means getting rid of, and the leader is the first letter

parts.note: a holster is a case holding a pistol

explanation.surface: An old soldier, sent off by his commander, kept his gun in its case and died in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an elderly person, an old hand or veteran.

clue.text: Middle Eastern city that is built up with dry environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the word for dry goes round the other piece

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: in a down clue built up means written upwards, so reading backwards

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A city has been built up in arid surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon, a city in the Middle East.

clue.text: 13 down's woman harbouring classy derrière, keeping the nation hot

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the word for woman holds the rest

parts.note: a lady is a woman
U means upper-class

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for derrière holds nation and hot

parts.note: derrière is French for the rear, the backside
a land is a nation

explanation.surface: A double act's lady friend has a posh backside and keeps the country warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were the Anglo-American comedy duo, so a double act (13 down). The 's on 13 down reads as has, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy were the most famous comic double act of early Hollywood.

clue.text: Responsibility round dawn?

definitions.meaning: a duty or burden that falls on someone
when the round of drinks is our treat, and when an idea dawns on someone, it falls on them

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on phrases: a round of drinks that is on us is ours to pay, and when realisation dawns, it dawns on us.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty, the responsibility that lies with someone.

clue.text: Golden snake's first off, turning with us through the trees

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, meaning formed of or full of trees

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the gold and snake pieces read backwards together

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the first letter of the snake is taken off

parts.note: the cobra is a venomous snake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golden snake, losing its head, twists alongside us through a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses gold and the headless snake as one run, giving ARBORO; 'first off' removes the cobra's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborous means formed by or relating to trees, so describes what is among the woods.

clue.text: See 15
As one 14 said: "Go back inside!"

indicators.note: inside means within, so the reversed word goes into the other piece

parts.note: 14 across is THAI, which said aloud sounds like tie, and to tie is to tether

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the word go is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia tells another person to go back indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 across answer, said aloud, sounds like 'tie', so the tie synonym is wanted rather than the Asian; 'back' reverses go before 'inside' puts it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as one means doing it jointly, all at once with others.

clue.text: Loves bread, or especially sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Someone loves bread, and sandwiches in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone or something is to love it deeply.
